docs.text: A couple of years ago, the whole row of houses facing the lake got pummelled by waves and they got encased in ice. So yeah, not so smart! (Photo from CNN)

This is Lake Huron in the Winter Time. Growing up as kids remember these going out in the lake for miles, also remember some of them being 15' high and go for miles and miles. Had one year we could skate for miles and miles on the ice. Guessing some followers here have never seen this before.
Didn’t skate at all on Go Skate Day but saw a concert on Lake Michigan with the good homie I started skating with 20+ years ago so maybe I did skate
The kids had an amazing time skating outdoors at the Sleeping Giant Provincial Park while Geoff’s I walked along Lake Superior.

My boss said that as a kid, she would sometimes hit pockets of water within the ice & fall through that another lower layer of ice. Skating indoors is a maybe, skating outdoors is a no, skating on the Great Lakes is a big old hell no

Indeed. And in North America, people used to race with sledges with sails on the Great Lakes. Worth a try, those locomotives. And the 19th-century engravings of roller skates with one big wheel, like a young bicycle wheel, used to fill me with longing. Now, I wish just for icy ponds again.
As a kid in western New York, we did that on farm ponds so we could skate. I have skated on Lake Erie a few times when it was flat enough. Now days they don't have enough consistently cold weather.

Very real. They still send out constant reminders to the students not to walk out on the ice buildup on the shores of Lake Ontario. It looks solid, but it often isn't, and if you fall in, that's basically it.
I remember those days. I lived in a forest near Lake Ontario when I was young and there were ponds that would freeze over to skate on. Looks fun.
Growing up near Lake Ontario I remember these more traditional ice boats on the frozen lake-adjacent bays in the winter but never an antique boat with metal skis applied.
As someone that grew up on the shores of Lake Ontario, you NEVER want to walk on the ice on that lake, unless of course you have a death wish.
Photographer Warns of Danger as People Walk on Icy Lake Michigan

Luge does look really cool! Bobsled, too.
I learned how to ice skate when I was about 3, on Lake Erie. I had little double bladed skates. So skating came fairly easily to me.
